parts.latex:
The diagram shows the graph $y=f(x)$.

\exfigure{1628_q10_1}

The point $Q$ is a horizontal point of inflection.

Let $A(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^x f(t)\,dt$.

How many points of inflection does the graph $y=A(x)$ have?

Definite integrals.reason: No integral is evaluated; only FTC A'(x)=f(x) and inflection reasoning are used.

solutions.latex:
By the fundamental theorem of calculus, $A'(x)=f(x)$, so $A''(x)=f'(x)$.

$A(x)$ has a point of inflection where $A''(x)=f'(x)$ changes sign, that is, at each turning point of $y=f(x)$.

At $Q$, $f'(x)=0$ but does not change sign, so $Q$ gives no inflection of $A$.

$y=f(x)$ has three turning points (a minimum, a maximum and a minimum), so $y=A(x)$ has 3 points of inflection.

parts.latex: Given that $f(x) = \displaystyle\int_2^x \dfrac{1}{1+t^3}\,dt$, what is the value of $f'(2)$?

solutions.latex:
By the fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\int_2^x \dfrac{1}{1+t^3}\,dt\right] = \dfrac{1}{1+x^3}$$

Hence:

$$f'(2) = \dfrac{1}{1+2^3} = \dfrac{1}{9}$$

So option C is correct.
